rubric.evidence: Verified on 2026-11-27 against MDN @container (301 -> HTTP 200 at /Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@container): MDN defines a name-only container query as `@container <container-name> { ... }` with NO query condition at all ('If only a container-name value is included...'). The stub's lede and Example row conflate this with container style queries (`@container sidebar style(--variant: compact)`), which already worked without `container-type`.
H1 'CSS Name-only Container Queries' matches Chrome 148 listing; declared ChromeStatus row links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5184267522015232; breadcrumb links /v148/.

Honest MDN redirect stub (exempt from reference-contract.json): MDN @container explicitly covers name-only container queries (linking the Container Queries guide section `#name-only_container_queries`), formal syntax, Specifications, and Browser compatibility.

Describes removing `container-type` requirement for style queries rather than the actual Chrome 148 feature — omitting the `<container-condition>` entirely so `@container sidebar { ... }` matches any descendant of a named container.
The inline example `@container sidebar style(--variant: compact) { ... }` demonstrates a named style query rather than a name-only container query (`@container sidebar { ... }`).
States Chrome 148 (desktop + Android) shipping and defers full BCD matrix to MDN @container.

Live check on 2026-11-27: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@container returns HTTP 301 redirecting to HTTP 200 at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@container. All external anchors carry target='_blank' rel='noopener' and all citations are directly linked.
Single <main>, single <h1>, sequential h2 headings, <header class='lede-block'>, and <footer class='byline'>. Minor legacy stub gap: .doc-table omits <caption> and <th scope='row'>.
Uses /public/styles.css with viewport meta; recorded desktop:ok and mobile:ok in responsive-support.json (agent-reviewed 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 screenshots on 2026-10-10).
